segments.text: Hey there, fellow agilists! Welcome  back to our YouTube channel. Today,
we're diving into a topic that's absolutely  essential for every software development team:
Backlog Prioritization! In this short  video, I’ll try to explain the general
concepts of backlog prioritization and I  will also show you one very powerful and
simple technique how to quickly determine  the priority of backlog items.
My name is Vladimir, I am an agile  coach, and this is Practical Agile.
Why Prioritize? It all starts with understanding  that our time and resources are limited.
You all probably know this situation. Your team  is fully utilized, working on many complex
features and yet another batch of requests from  an important customer arrives. So, what should
you do? You need to start prioritizing your work,  as it is obvious that you can't do it all at once,
right? And the reason why we are prioritizing  is to make sure that even with our limited
resources we are still delivering the maximum  possible value for both users and the business.
Setting priority always requires you to  evaluate multiple criteria. You cannot
use just one criterion for prioritization.  It is similar to being a captain of a ship,
who needs to decide which direction to sail. A  captain needs to consider things like wind speed,
currents, fuel, load and the destination,  right? Well, in software development,
we are considering things like business value,  effort, risk, and alignment with our strategy.
It's like plotting our development  team course for success!
There are many prioritization techniques  you can use, like MoSCoW, Kano model,
weighted scoring, opportunity vs cost, RICE  scoring and so on. You can use all of them,
but here comes the real magic - WSJF! WSJF stands  for Weighted Shortest Job First and it's like the
Swiss Army knife of prioritization techniques. It  allows you to quickly determine relative priority
of your backlog items. It is based on a calculated  prioritization score, which is a ratio of so
called “Cost of Delay” to a Job size. The Cost  of Delay is calculated using multiple inputs. It
takes into account Business Value, because, well,  we all love happy customers and revenue, don't we?
Another part of the Cost of Delay is Time  Criticality, because some tasks are more
urgent than others. We also need to include  Risk Reduction to avoid potential pitfalls.
And finally, we need to factor in Job Size – which  is the effort required to get things done. Put all
these together, rate them according to your best  knowledge on a scale from 1 to 10 and boom! We've
got a formula for prioritization score that allows  us to quickly and correctly order our backlog!
As I mentioned earlier, an important aspect  of backlog prioritization is that it needs to
be aligned with your strategy. But what does it  exactly mean? Think of it this way - our software
development is like a treasure hunt, where our  vision and mission are the "X marks on the map".
By aligning our backlog with our  organization's big-picture goals,
we are making sure we follow the path  on the map that leads to the treasure!
Also keep in mind that our team is usually  part of some business entity, and as such,
we're not here just to build some software  for pleasure. We're here to create value
that's perfectly aligned with our mission  and vision! That’s why you are getting paid!
Now, let's talk about teamwork! Imagine a  game of soccer. If you are a soccer player,
you need to know who's where  during the game, right?
The same goes for communicating your priorities  inside your organization. By openly communicating
your priorities, everybody is on the same  page, playing together for a winning goal!
Remember, backlog prioritization isn't  a one-time thing. It's a continuous
activity that evolves as our project does. With  regular check-ins, we inspect, tweak, adjust,
and refine our priorities to stay in perfect  sync with our goals and actual situation.
So, there you have it! We've explored the  why, how, and what of backlog prioritization.
Remember, it's all about making those  tough choices to deliver maximum value.
Whether you're in software development, business,
or just curious about how things work, the  ability to prioritize well is a game-changer!
If you're as excited as I am about  leveling up your agile skills,
hit that Subscribe button and give us a thumbs  up. And don't forget to leave a comment sharing
your thoughts on backlog prioritization. Until  next time, happy coding, and stay curious!
See you in the next video!
